problem: Foundation navigation policies (NavDP, NoMaD) are memory-free and wander when the goal is not visible. Memory-based zero-shot methods rely on dense RGB-D maps or object graphs that are costly to build and brittle to rearrangements and dynamic obstacles.
motivation: Humans navigate with sparse visual memories for coarse global guidance plus continuous local replanning. Combining a compact memory with a robust pretrained local policy could give long-horizon reasoning and obstacle robustness without dense 3D reconstruction. Image-goal viewpoint alignment is also weak in existing policies.
key_idea: Plan node-level paths over a sparse, region-centric Sparse Spatial Memory Graph (SMG) using hybrid keyframe and object retrieval, and execute them with a NavDP foundation policy that is enhanced by a VGGT-adapter, running global re-localization and local control at different frequencies.
insight: The component ablation shows the sparse memory does most of the work: SMG raises NavDP from 24.70/12.60 to 74.04/56.14 SR/SPL, and the VGGT-adapter adds a further 4.5 SR to 78.50/59.27. Hybrid retrieval beats either keyframe-only (73.52/52.90) or object-only (72.20/52.79) retrieval. Overly sparse graphs (d=2.0 m) hurt SPL sharply (46.89), indicating that viewpoint diversity and connectivity matter. Under obstacle insertion, the decoupled design keeps performance stable, since the local policy handles obstacles without depending on the map.
method: Sparse Spatial Memory Graph: Farthest-point sampling on posed tour camera poses gives nodes (radius r); edges come from temporal adjacency. Each node stores its 3D center P, N_f diverse keyframe DINOv2 CLS embeddings F, and object embeddings O from Grounded-SAM plus DINOv2 (CLS and mean patch features, merged by a cosine-similarity threshold τ).

Hybrid image-node retrieval: Keyframe cosine similarity (max over the node's keyframes) selects top-N_o candidate nodes. Same-category object similarity is then averaged, and the node with the highest mean of the two scores wins. It is used to localize both I_obs and I_goal.
Node-level A* planning: A* over SMG edges from v_obs to v_goal, with a final node v_K appended to represent the exact goal image.

VGGT-adapter: VGGT features of the observation and the goal image are average-pooled, flattened and concatenated, then projected by an MLP into the policy embedding space. The result is concatenated with the NavDP visual condition tokens.
Node-based local navigation: NavDP runs in point-goal mode between intermediate nodes (P_k) and switches to image-goal mode for the final segment toward I_goal.
Dual-scale loop: Global re-localization and A* re-planning every T_g steps, or when the visual-confidence score drops or edges are blocked. Local control runs at a faster T_l frequency.

setting.backbone: NavDP diffusion policy (pretrained) + VGGT-adapter MLP (trained); DINOv2-ViT-L/14, Grounded-SAM-2 and VGGT frozen
setting.training_data: NavDP pretrained on its own large-scale data; the VGGT-adapter is fine-tuned on source data only (details in the appendix, not provided); no training in target scenes; SMG built from posed tour demonstrations
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (memory RGB only, no depth for the map); goal image
setting.action_space: waypoint / trajectory chunks from NavDP (point-goal and image-goal modes)
setting.privileged: posed tour demonstrations of each test scene for building SMG (pre-exploration); node 3D positions used as point goals

numbers.extra: pre-collected posed tour for memory; success radius 1.0 m, 500 steps
numbers.evidence: Table 1 InstanceImageNav on HM3D: MG-Nav SMG (RGB) 78.5 / 59.3

numbers_note: Split names for HM3D (val-unseen) and MP3D (test) are inferred from the descriptions; the paper only says validation scenes and testing scenes.
results: MG-Nav gets 78.5/59.3 SR/SPL on HM3D InstanceImageNav, beating GaussNav (72.5/57.8) and BSC-Nav (71.4/57.2), and 83.77/57.15 on MP3D ImageNav, beating FGPrompt-EF (77.71/51.09). With 10 inserted obstacles, SR falls only from 73.53 to 68.63, while UniGoal drops from 56.43 to 44.21 and BSC-Nav from 25.49 to 7.84.
limitations: Requires a pre-collected posed tour demonstration of each scene to build SMG, and needs simulator poses.
Evaluated only in Habitat simulation on two benchmarks with no real robot; robustness tests use only 100 episodes and random obstacle insertion, not real rearrangement of the scene.
Depends on many frozen large models (Grounded-SAM, DINOv2, VGGT, NavDP); the baselines ViNT, GNM, NoMaD and NavDP are the authors' re-implementations.
